msg: Run r_mock_demo on Token Factory Sandboxes · 50 slots · budget 5.0% LUT-equivalent area
Baseline: 860,730 cycles; tm_dot_prod (tm_dot.h:26-37) is 95.7% of the measured region

Ultra on root: tm_dot_prod is 95.7% of the measured region: per 8 elements, 8 byte loads, 8 multiplies and 8 adds, with the multiply-add chain serial on PicoRV32. Inputs are 4-byte aligned, so word loads can feed packed lanes. Requant (2.6%) is in main.c, which is not patchable. Proposing packed dots, an accumulator and two cheap hedges.

proposal.title: Packed int8 dot product
proposal.rationale: tm_dot_prod is 95.7% of the measured region. Every four MACs cost eight byte loads, four multiplies and four adds; packing four int8 lanes per register turns those 16 instructions into two word loads, one dot4.s8 and one add.

proposal.title: Dual-lane int8 dot product
proposal.rationale: Half the multipliers of a four-lane dot for a bit more than half the gain. A cheap point on the area curve in case the four-lane tree does not fit the budget.

proposal.title: Dual int8 multiply into packed int16
proposal.rationale: Two products per instruction with no adder tree, so it stays off the critical path. The kernel still adds the two halves in software.

proposal.title: Pipelined packed int8 dot (2 cycles)
proposal.rationale: Same semantics as a single-cycle four-lane dot, with a register between the multipliers and the adder tree. A hedge in case the combinational tree lands on the critical path and costs Fmax.

proposal.title: Mixed-sign dot product (u8 × s8)
proposal.rationale: If activations are post-ReLU they are non-negative; an unsigned activation lane drops the sign extension and matches common int8 inference ISAs.

proposal.title: Accumulating dot4 (internal accumulator)
proposal.rationale: After packing, one add per dot remains in the loop and every dot depends on the sum register. Keeping the running sum inside the unit removes both.

proposal.title: Horizontal int8 lane sum
proposal.rationale: Sums four signed bytes in one step. TinyMaix pairs int8 dots with an input-sum term for asymmetric zero points; a lane sum removes three adds per word there.

proposal.title: Packed int16 dot product
proposal.rationale: A reusable 16-bit dot for int16 layers. On int8 data the kernel must sign-extend bytes into halfwords first, so the gain here is modest.

msg: Beam step 1: keeping n1 dot4.s8 3.77×, n4 dot4p.s8 3.59×, n2 dot2.s8 2.14× (B = 3)

Ultra on n1: With dot4.s8 the loop is 2 lw + 1 dot4 + 1 add per 4 MACs plus loop control. The add and the sum dependency are the lever left; an internal accumulator removes them but costs about 2% LUT-eq, which is more than the 1.84% of headroom. Trying three accumulator designs, a fused load (if the slot allows it) and a tail helper.

proposal.title: Accumulating dot4 (internal accumulator)
proposal.rationale: After packing, one add per dot remains in the loop and every dot depends on the sum register. Keeping the running sum inside the unit removes both.

proposal.title: Accumulating dot4, narrow accumulator
proposal.rationale: A 512-element int8 dot stays within 24 bits, so a narrow accumulator should do and saves about half a percent of area against the 32-bit design.

proposal.title: Accumulating dot4, carry-save partials
proposal.rationale: Keeps the accumulator in carry-save form so the carry chain leaves the critical path, and reuses dot4.s8's multiplier tree to stay inside the budget.

proposal.title: dot4 with post-increment loads
proposal.rationale: Loads dominate what is left of the loop. Fusing both word loads and the pointer bumps into the dot would remove three instructions per dot4.

proposal.title: Masked tail dot (1–3 lanes)
proposal.rationale: Handles sizes not divisible by four without the scalar tail loop. No gain at size 512, but it keeps the patched kernel general for other layer shapes.

msg: Ultra on n2: dot2.s8 leaves half the multiplies in software. A four-lane dot fits beside it (about 3.1%), and a dual-lane accumulator is the cheapest accumulator there is.

proposal.title: Packed int8 dot product
proposal.rationale: tm_dot_prod is 95.7% of the measured region. Every four MACs cost eight byte loads, four multiplies and four adds; packing four int8 lanes per register turns those 16 instructions into two word loads, one dot4.s8 and one add.

proposal.title: Accumulating dual-lane dot
proposal.rationale: dot2.s8 with the running sum kept inside the unit: the cheapest accumulator that could fit beside it.

proposal.title: Dual int8 multiply into packed int16
proposal.rationale: Two products per instruction with no adder tree, so it stays off the critical path. The kernel still adds the two halves in software.

proposal.title: Pack two int8 into int16 lanes
proposal.rationale: Builds sign-extended int16 lane pairs from byte data in one step, for int16-lane helpers stacked on this CPU.

proposal.title: Packed int16 dot product
proposal.rationale: A reusable 16-bit dot for int16 layers. On int8 data the kernel must sign-extend bytes into halfwords first, so the gain here is modest.
